blockingFindings.summary: One-to-one entity matching incorrectly consumes a valid candidate across relation endpoint slots.
blockingFindings.evidence: _endpoint_resolution stores matched candidate IDs in a global used set while iterating relation endpoints. In the review case g1->g2 and g1->g3 with three exact typed-span candidates, the scorer returned resolved=3 and wrong=1 instead of resolved=4 and wrong=0.
blockingFindings.impact: Any entity participating in more than one relation is misclassified after its first use. The gold-relations integrity control and endpoint denominators can fail on ordinary graph topology even when every candidate and relation is correct.
blockingFindings.requiredRemediation: Build a one-to-one mapping once between distinct gold entities and predicted candidates, then reuse that mapping for every relation endpoint occurrence. Add shared-source, shared-target, relation-cycle and repeated-endpoint denominator tests.

blockingFindings.summary: Occurrence content is asserted by metadata but not proven from the runtime source slice.
blockingFindings.evidence: EvidenceContext contains sourceLength and TriggerOccurrence.quoteDigest, but neither the scorer nor an offline materializer derives a digest from source[start:end]. The content-mismatch test changes the supplied quoteDigest; it does not test a source slice whose content disagrees with otherwise valid metadata.
blockingFindings.impact: Malformed server-owned occurrence metadata can still claim a valid quote digest for an unrelated in-bounds span, so source-to-occurrence custody is not yet demonstrated before preregistration.
blockingFindings.requiredRemediation: Implement and test a server-owned runtime-only occurrence materializer that derives the occurrence digest from the Unicode code-point source slice, passes only sanitized span/digest metadata to reports, and fails closed on source-slice, normalization, boundary or digest mismatch.

constraints: Preserve all v1-v4 packages and review artifacts as immutable history.
Do not preregister, freeze an execution package, authorize provider execution or inspect held-out data from RM-20D.
A superseding offline package requires a separate owner re-review.
